instructions: pip is a creature on a stead node. Ask it in plain words; it answers when it next works. Your words are a note in its conversation: they start no work and grant nothing. On this machine you may also open things for the keeper through it: show, shown, arrange and withdraw set things out beside pip's conversation or in windows of their own in the keeper's app. The tools were written for pip and are lent to you as they are, so read their "you", "yours" and "your conversation" as pip. What you open rises from the porch unless you name another place, carries a small square in a colour kept for your client's name, and counts against pip's limits; pip and the keeper are told. The keeper is the person pip works with. A terminal or a screen acts on the keeper's machine, so the keeper is asked each time.

tools.name: arrange
tools.description: Here "you" is pip, the creature you work through. Lay out your windows outside, at any sizes in any combination. Give a shape (grid, columns, rows, lead-and-cards, lead-and-stack, split, board), how the things relate (sequence, alternatives, tasks, notes), or a spot for each, {seats: {"<id or title>": "left-two-thirds"}}; with none of them the app chooses. lead names the one that gets the large spot and side where it stands. panes picks which things: all your windows outside when left out, and "all" also brings out what sits beside your conversation. {back: true} undoes your last arrangement. mark changes the word on a window, {mark: {"<id>": "done"}} or {mark: {"<id>": {text: "done", tone: "good"}}}, and signal raises or lowers its outline; either can go alone. {keep: "<name>"} keeps what you have out, and where each thing stands, as a scene by that name (up to twelve); {scene: "<name>"} sets a kept scene out again, and {forget: "<name>"} lets one go. It moves only the app's own windows, never takes focus, and leaves alone what the keeper placed. The answer says where everything now stands.

panes.description: Which things to arrange, in the order they should read: each by its id, or by the ref or title you showed it with. Leave it out for everything you have outside, or say "all" for everything you have out, beside the conversation too.

shape.description: A layout by name: grid (equal seats), columns (tall, side by side), rows (wide, stacked), lead-and-cards (one large, the rest as cards around it), lead-and-stack (one large beside a column of the rest), split (two large side by side, the rest as cards beneath) or board (columns of cards, for tasks).

relation.description: How the things relate, leaving the layout to the console: sequence, alternatives, tasks or notes.

seats.description: A seat for each pane you place, as {"<id or title>": seat} or [{id, seat}], with seats written as in show: a named seat, lattice lines, or {x, y, w, h}.

lead.description: The pane that should have the large seat.

side.description: Where the lead stands when the console lays the panes out: left (the default), right, top or bottom. The rest take the other side. It goes with a shape, a relation or neither, and with or without lead: unnamed, the first pane leads.

mark.description: The word or two on a window, by its id or title: {"<id>": "chosen"}, or with a tone (neutral (the default), good, caution or bad), {"<id>": {text: "chosen", tone: "good"}}. An empty string or null clears it.

signal.description: How much a pane wants the keeper, drawn as an outline, by its id or title: {"<id>": "needs-you"} outlines it in amber until it is answered, {"<id>": "critical"} in red, and null lowers it. Critical needs why, goes only on what you set out yourself, and you may hold one at a time; only you or the keeper lower it. It moves nothing, and goes alone or with any arrangement.

why.description: With signal, the one sentence the keeper reads on the pane you raise: what you need from them, or what is wrong. Critical needs it.

rest.description: What becomes of your other windows outside, the ones this arrangement does not name: stay (the default with seats) leaves them where they stand; beside steps them back beside the conversation, still out, so the panes you name stand alone.

back.description: true puts your windows back in the seats they had before your last arrangement, wherever those seats came from: the way back after you rearranged. Say it again to go back further. It goes alone or with a mood.

over.description: room (the default) arranges on the stage, the room beside the console; display arranges across the whole screen, where your windows may stand over the console. Say display when the keeper speaks of the screen, as in "a quarter of the screen".

mood.description: How the panes move into place, as motion only: one of show's moods; left out, your temperament's if you have one, else brisk. The answer names the mood it moved with.

keep.description: Keep what you have out as a scene by this name, as it stands now: each thing, and its seat outside or its place beside your conversation. With panes, only those. Keeping a name you already keep replaces it. You keep up to twelve scenes.

from.description: With keep, the place in the stead the scene belongs to, named as show's from names one (a project or folder you have worked in, by name or path); pressing that place sets the scene out. Left out, a scene whose things all rose from one project belongs to it.

scene.description: Set out a scene you kept, by its name: each thing again where it stood. It goes alone, or with a mood.

forget.description: Let a scene you kept go, by its name. Nothing that is out moves.

tools.name: ask
tools.description: Leave pip a note in plain words, or poll an earlier ask by its handle. The note starts no work and carries no approval; pip answers when it next works, and the answer comes back on a poll.

text.description: Plain words for the creature. They wait in its conversation as a note.

handle.description: The handle an earlier ask returned, to read the answer.

tools.name: deliveries
tools.description: The report lines pip's finished threads and chores delivered to its conversation, oldest first.

after.description: The entryId of the last delivery already read; only later ones come back.

tools.name: show
tools.description: Here "you" is pip, the creature you work through. Set out something for the keeper, the person you work with, to see in their app: a file, a diff, a report, a thread, a chore, a link, a short markdown note, or one of the app's own panes by name (sessions, arcs, files, context, memory, needs-you, permissions, mcp, workspaces, workshop, mills, parcels, bots, campaigns, themes, posture, stead, terminal, screen). Reach for it when you have changed what the keeper asked about, or they ask to see something or be walked through it. It opens beside your conversation, or in a window of its own with where "outside"; seat picks its spot ("left-half", "top-right") and shape lays out several at once. keep names what this call sets out as a scene, so arrange with scene sets it out again. A terminal or a screen acts on the keeper's machine, so the keeper is asked every time, in a scene too. It rises from a place: your workshop, unless from names another (the porch, the storehouse, the mill, a project or folder you have worked in by name or path, another creature's workshop) or something of yours already out, which it grows from. Showing the same thing again changes it in place; a note with the same title is the same note. mark puts a word or two on it, with a tone; signal outlines it when your work waits on the keeper (needs-you) or something is broken (critical, with why). Every answer gives its id, for arrange and withdraw.

ref.description: Which one: a workspace path, a change-set id, a report id, a session id, a chore id, a url, the note's own markdown (at most 2000 characters), or a pane's name: sessions, arcs, files, context, memory, needs-you, permissions, mcp, workspaces, workshop, mills, parcels, bots, campaigns, themes, posture, stead, terminal, screen.

what.description: The thing to set out, or a list of up to twelve set out together. Each may carry its own seat, why, weight, from, mark, tone and signal.

why.description: One sentence the keeper reads with it: why it matters now.

where.description: beside (the default) keeps it by your conversation; outside gives it a window.

seat.description: Its spot outside, on a 12 by 12 grid: a name (full, left-half, right-half, top-half, bottom-half, left-third, middle-third, right-third, left-two-thirds, right-two-thirds, left-quarter, right-quarter, top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right, center, top-third, bottom-third), lines such as "columns 4 to 8, rows 0 to 6", or {x, y, w, h}. Leave it out and the app chooses.

shape.description: Lays out what this call sets out, in windows outside: grid, columns, rows, lead-and-cards, lead-and-stack, split or board.

weight.description: lead, support or aside: who gets the large spot. With from, lead drills in.

mood.description: How it moves in, motion only: calm (slow and soft), brisk (the default, plain), eager (quick, close together), playful (out of turn, in a rhythm), urgent (all at once, fast), decisive (all at once, landing firmly) or tentative (a little slow, one at a time with pauses, landing lightly). Left out, it moves with your temperament, if you have one.

mark.description: A word or two on it while it is out, such as "draft" or "done", or {text, tone}. arrange changes it later.

tone.description: The mark's tone: neutral (the default), good, caution or bad.

signal.description: needs-you (amber) when your work waits on the keeper; critical (red) only when something is broken or about to be lost, with why; null lowers it. Use it rarely.

rung.description: Beside your conversation, how much attention it asks: lantern (least), card (the default), unfold or stage (most).

size.description: card, readable or working: how large it first opens.

until.description: When it goes: seen (the default: it stays until the keeper puts it away), rests (when this conversation goes quiet), a time from now such as "10 minutes", or an ISO 8601 time.

from.description: Where it rises from: a place (your workshop, the porch, the storehouse, the mill, a project or folder you have worked in by name or path, another creature's workshop such as "pip's workshop"), or something of yours already out (by id or title), which it then grows from.

keep.description: A name to keep what this call sets out under, as a scene: each thing and where it stands. arrange with scene sets it out again. Keeping a name you already keep replaces it; you keep up to twelve.

tools.name: shown
tools.description: Here "you" is pip, the creature you work through. List what is open for the keeper, whoever opened it, one JSON line each: id, what, place (where in the stead it rose from), from (the id of what it grew from, or null), where it stands now (beside your conversation, outside in its own window with its seat such as "left-half", or inside the app), by (who put it there last: you, the keeper or the app), mark, tone, signal, state and when it goes. origin keeper means the keeper opened it; agent names an agent that set it out through you. A line says how much room your windows have outside, and a last line names the scenes you keep. It changes nothing. Use the ids with from, arrange and withdraw, and the scene names with arrange.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Where pip is now: working, at the porch (waiting on its keeper), back (a delivery is in), idle, or paused.

tools.name: withdraw
tools.description: Here "you" is pip, the creature you work through. Close what you set out, beside your conversation or outside, and it goes back where it came from. Name it by the id show gave, or by its title or ref; a list closes several, and "all" with except closes everything but those. It will not close what the keeper pinned or opened, a critical someone else raised, or anything not yours. What grew from it stays out, and closing a window that drilled in steps back out to its parent. It moves only the app's own windows, never the computer. mood says how it leaves.

id.description: What to take back: an id, or the ref or title you showed it with. A list takes back several, and "all" takes back everything of yours that is out.

except.description: With id "all", what stays out: ids, refs or titles.

mood.description: How it leaves, as motion only: one of show's moods. Leave it out and it leaves with your temperament, if you have one, else in the mood it arrived with.
